A lot of people here aren't fond of the whole "being defined by the enemy" thing here, but to me it seems like a pretty straightforward and easy-to-understand way to describe what my beliefs are.

I'm not sure if it's semantically true. Definitions of racism tend to hinge on the word "superiority." If you go to dictionary.com, you get this:

1. a belief or doctrine that inherent differences among the various human racial groups determine cultural or individual achievement, usually involving the idea that one's own race is superior and has the right to dominate others or that a particular racial group is inferior to the others.

2. a policy, system of government, etc., based upon or fostering such a doctrine; discrimination.

3. hatred or intolerance of another race or other races.

This from Oxford Dictionaries:

  1. Prejudice, discrimination, or antagonism directed against someone of a different race based on the belief that one's own race is superior.

1.1 The belief that all members of each race possess characteristics, abilities, or qualities specific to that race, especially so as to distinguish it as inferior or superior to another race or races.

And here's Merriam-Webster:

1: a belief that race is the primary determinant of human traits and capacities and that racial differences produce an inherent superiority of a particular race 2

a : a doctrine or political program based on the assumption of racism and designed to execute its principles

b : a political or social system founded on racism

3: racial prejudice or discrimination

There's a bit of variation here. Dictionary.com says "a belief or doctrine that inherent differences among the various human racial groups determine cultural or individual achievement..." and then adds 'usually' to describe the belief in superiority of races, meaning it's not strictly true that you have to believe in racial superiority. Its other two definitions are "a policy, system of government, etc., based upon or fostering such a doctrine; discrimination" (more or less a repeat of the first) and "hatred or intolerance of another race or other races." I wouldn't say I particularly hate nonwhites. It's not like they chose where they would be born and then checked off a box to be part of the Jews' plan to destabilize the West. And as for tolerance, maybe I want to marry within my own race and avoid getting entangled in deep relationships with Blacks, but I've had plenty of nonwhite coworkers and acquaintances who I've gotten along with on the surface just fine. Compared to my liberal ex-classmates who grew up in a six-figure median income town, I probably interact with minorities far more normally than they do, and I wouldn't call them racists (hypocrites, maybe).

Oxford Dictionaries and Merriam-Webster seem to be a bit more dependent on the idea that racism require a belief in inherent superiority rather than a belief in inherent differences. Oxford's 1.1 definition is a bit like dictionary.com's first. And Merriam-Webster seems to outright assume a belief of superiority, though maybe with some leeway depending on how you define 'prejudice' and 'discrimination' in its third definition.

So why the nitpicking over the word "superiority?" Because there's a difference between a belief in inherent differences and inherent superiority. And even in something like the IQ gap, the idea of superiority can get a bit philosophical. I'll say Blacks at large are genetically predisposed to be less intelligent than Whites, but I wouldn't necessarily say that means Whites are superior, because intelligence isn't an absolute good or a universal determinant of worth. There are plenty of intelligent people that become miserable cynical assholes that do nothing with their life, and there are plenty of dumb people who go out and accomplish things with their straightforward retard-level motivation. Perhaps it means that whites as a whole are superior at being members of the societies that they originally built for themselves (i.e. The West); and that Blacks as a whole are, in conjunction with factors such as a deep-seated cultural divide and humans' natural tribalistic tendencies, never going to meet the lofty idea of integration that race optimists tend to push. But does that mean that a white's life is worth more than a black's in every part of the world? Or that I think Orientals are better than Whites because their genetic intelligence is higher than ours? Nah. Maybe Whites and East Asians are superior at building lawful communities and white-collar work environments. But they're not superior at being athletes in high-testosterone athletics, or dealing with the challenges of surviving in a society where women are more likely to be raped than to learn how to read or where the national currency has a serious risk of losing its value overnight.
